mainTopic: Yoma 64b: Whether a living animal that becomes unfit can be permanently pushed aside (בעלי חיים נדחין) when one of the two Yom Kippur goats dies. רבא shows the משנה fits רב and the ברייתא fits רבי יוחנן, and then a challenge is raised against רב from רבי יהודה.
overview: When one of the two goats of יום כפור dies after the lottery, רב and רבי יוחנן disagree about the goat that is left. רב holds בעלי חיים אינן נדחין: the survivor is not permanently disqualified and can still be used. רבי יוחנן holds בעלי חיים נדחין: the survivor is pushed aside for good, and a goat from a new pair is used instead. The amud opens with the last line of רבי יוסי's ברייתא, and then רבא shows that the משנה's wording supports רב while a ברייתא, reading the verse יעמד חי, supports רבי יוחנן. Next the גמרא challenges רב from רבי יהודה's ruling that the שעיר המשתלח must die if the blood spills. רב answers that he follows the חכמים, not רבי יהודה. The גמרא then asks what רבי יהודה and the חכמים would argue about according to רבי יוחנן, and רבא simply concedes that the משנה reads better like רב. Finally, the גמרא draws an inference from the משנה that a private חטאת in such a case is left to die. It explains this easily for רבי יוחנן using a ruling of רבי אבא in the name of רב, and the challenge against רב continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of רבי יוסי's teaching: use the second animal if it is better
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes a ברייתא quoted just before. רבי יוסי holds that the first animal should be used, unless the second one is of better quality.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the second one was better than it, he should bring that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that began on the previous amud. In it, רבי יוסי says the first animal gets priority unless the second is of better quality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full ברייתא is about someone whose קרבן got lost, who set aside a replacement, and then found the original. רבי יוסי says the מצוה is with the first animal (מצוה בראשון). The one exception is when the second animal is higher quality. The גמרא uses this to show how רבי יוסי would decide which goat to use.

keyTerms.meaning: He should bring it (as the offering)
The מצוה is with the first one (רבי יוסי's principle)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a quote from the previous section, not a new statement. Read it as the tail of רבי יוסי's ברייתא.

phrases.english: And if the second one was superior to it
phrases.notes: The second animal is better quality than the first.

phrases.english: he brings that one.
phrases.notes: Normally the first animal is preferred, but here the better quality one wins out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיָה הַשֵּׁנִי מוּבְחָר מִמֶּנּוּ — יְבִיאֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא of רבי יוסי begun earlier.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's view on which of two available animals gets priority
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about a lost and found חטאת

steps.title: רבא: the משנה's wording fits רב, the ברייתא's wording fits רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבא states his thesis. The wording of the משנה supports רב, and the wording of a ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה's wording fits רב, and the ברייתא's wording fits רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא announces that each side of the מחלוקת has some textual support. This sets up the next two steps, where he will show each proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not settle the מחלוקת here. He points out that each opinion can find a precise reading (דיוק) in a different source. The משנה leans toward רב, and a ברייתא leans toward רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise / the exact wording implies
A teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה

phrases.english: Rava said:
The mishna is precise in accordance with Rav,
and the baraita in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דַּיְקָא מַתְנִיתִין כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יוסי's view to finding textual support for רב and רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's wording supports רב (בעלי חיים אינן נדחין), and a ברייתא's wording supports רבי יוחנן (בעלי חיים נדחין).

steps.title: How the משנה's wording supports רב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה only says the new goat drawn 'for ה׳' replaces the dead one. That implies the original surviving goat keeps its status, which is רב's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה fits רב, because it teaches: 'If the one for ה׳ died, this one on which the lot for ה׳ fell shall stand in its place.' And the other goat stays as it was.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows his first proof. The משנה replaces only the goat that died, so the original surviving goat must still keep its role.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells us only that the new goat 'for ה׳' takes the dead goat's place. It says nothing about the old surviving goat losing its status. רבא reads that silence as meaning the old goat stays as it was (כדקאי קאי). That means it was not pushed aside, which matches רב: בעלי חיים אינן נדחין.

keyTerms.meaning: The lottery used to assign the two goats
Stays as it stood (its status is unchanged)

phrases.english: The mishna is in accordance with Rav, as it teaches:
If the one for God died,
this one upon which the lot for God came up
phrases.notes: A goat from the new pair.

phrases.english: shall stand in its stead,
and the other stands as it stood.
phrases.notes: רבא is drawing a conclusion: the surviving goat from the first pair keeps its job, so it isn't set aside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first half of רבא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the surviving goat is not permanently rejected
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'זה שעלה עליו הגורל לשם יתקיים תחתיו'

steps.title: How the ברייתא's wording supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks which 'second' goat is sent off to graze. Based on the verse יעמד חי, it answers that the goat whose partner died is not used, which matches רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא fits רבי יוחנן, because it teaches: 'The second one': I don't know if this means the second goat of the first pair or the second goat of the second pair. When the verse says 'It shall be stood alive,' it means not the one whose partner died.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows his second proof. The ברייתא learns from a verse that the goat left over from the first pair is not used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there are two pairs, one leftover goat is not needed and is sent off to graze. The ברייתא asks which one that is. It concludes that the goat whose partner died cannot be used, so the new pair's goat is used and the old survivor is the one sent off. That is exactly רבי יוחנן's view: the old survivor was permanently pushed aside (נדחה).

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know (opens a question the ברייתא will answer)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Second' here does not mean the second goat in time. It means the extra goat that is left over and not used.

phrases.english: The baraita is in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, as it teaches:
'The second' — I do not know
whether it is the second of the first pair
or the second of the second pair.
When it says 'It shall be stood alive,'
and not one whose partner died.
phrases.notes: So the survivor of the first pair is the one that is not used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second half of רבא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that the surviving goat is permanently rejected

steps.title: How does the verse show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the words יעמד חי teach that the goat whose partner died is excluded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא. Where in the verse do we see that the goat whose partner died is excluded? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the plain words of the verse mentions a partner dying. So the גמרא wants to know which detail in the verse carries the lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the implication? / How is this derived?

phrases.english: From where may it be inferred?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the ברייתא's verse-reading works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which feature of 'יעמד חי' excludes the goat whose partner died

steps.title: The future tense excludes a goat that already stood
steps.stepSummary: 'יעמד' is in the future tense: it 'shall be stood.' That excludes a goat that already stood before ה׳ with its partner that died.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It shall be stood alive': not one that already stood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the lesson comes from the future tense of the word יעמד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעמד means 'shall be stood,' describing a goat that has not yet been placed. The old survivor was already stood with its partner, which then died. So it does not fit the verse, and the scapegoat must come from the new pair. This completes the support for רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's silence about the old goat supports רב (it is not rejected). The ברייתא's reading of יעמד חי supports רבי יוחנן (it is rejected).

phrases.english: 'It shall be stood alive,'
phrases.notes: Notice the verb is in the future tense: 'it shall be' stood.

phrases.english: and not one that already stood.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The future tense of 'יעמד' excludes a goat that was already stood.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה. If the blood of the goat for ה׳ spills, the שעיר המשתלח must die. If the משתלח dies, the blood is poured out.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: And furthermore, רבי יהודה said: If the blood spilled, the scapegoat must die. If the scapegoat died, the blood must be poured out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ruling from the משנה. This sets up a challenge against רב in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה ties the two goats together: if one is lost, the other cannot be used either. The משתלח is left to die, and the blood is poured out. The גמרא is about to test this rule against the views of רב and רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood spilled (before it was sprinkled)

phrases.english: We learned: And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:
If the blood spilled, the scapegoat shall die;
if the scapegoat died, the blood shall be poured out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new source to test the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, losing one goat's role makes the other unusable: the scapegoat dies, or the blood is poured out.

steps.title: Challenge to רב: why must the scapegoat die?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's ruling fits רבי יוחנן, who says animals become rejected. But according to רב, the leftover משתלח should still be usable, so why must it die?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי יוחנן, who says living animals can be rejected; that is why the scapegoat must die. But for רב, who says living animals cannot be rejected, why must the scapegoat die?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב using רבי יהודה's ruling. According to רב the leftover goat should still be usable, so why must it die?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the משתלח was rejected when the blood spilled, so it is fitting that it is left to die. According to רב, a living animal is never permanently rejected. So the משתלח could simply be paired with a new goat for ה׳‎. רבי יהודה's ruling seems to contradict רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (sets up a contrast)
Living animals can be permanently rejected

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a direct test of רב's principle בעלי חיים אינן נדחין against an explicit משנה.

phrases.english: Granted according to Rabbi Yoḥanan,
who said living animals are rejected,
for that reason the scapegoat must die.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַב, דְּאָמַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵינָן נִדְחִין —
phrases.english: But according to Rav, who said living animals are not rejected,
why must the scapegoat die?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים נִדְחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling quoted in step 7 to attack רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's principle בעלי חיים אינן נדחין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משתלח is not rejected, it should still be usable with a new goat for ה׳. Yet רבי יהודה rules that it must die.

steps.title: רב follows the חכמים, not רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that his view was never based on רבי יהודה. He follows the חכמים, who hold that animals are not permanently rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: I did not say my rule according to רבי יהודה. When I said it, I said it according to the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 8 on רב's behalf. רב says he simply follows the other opinion, the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that once an animal is pushed off (דחוי), it stays rejected, so the leftover שעיר המשתלח must die. The חכמים disagree and hold that living animals are not permanently rejected. רב says his ruling, that the leftover goat can still be used, follows the חכמים, so רבי יהודה's ruling is no problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you. The גמרא is giving the answer someone would give in defense of his view.
The חכמים, the majority Sages who disagree with רבי יהודה
Rejection. Once an animal is disqualified, it stays disqualified.

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קָא אָמֵינָא.
phrases.english: I did not say it according to Rabbi Yehuda.
When I said it, it was according to the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by tying רב to the opposing opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution shift: the ruling belongs to a different תנא (the חכמים), not to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because רבי יהודה rules that the leftover משתלח must die, we might think רב is contradicted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה holds that animals are permanently rejected. The חכמים do not, and רב follows the חכמים.

steps.title: What do רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about according to רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: For רב, the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים is clear: whether animals are rejected. For רבי יוחנן it is unclear what they would argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רב: this is what רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about. But according to רבי יוחנן, what do they argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the question on רבי יוחנן. If everyone agrees animals are rejected, what is left for רבי יהודה and the חכמים to argue about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the two sides argue about whether animals can be permanently rejected. רבי יוחנן holds that even the חכמים agree the leftover goat is rejected and is sent to graze. If so, that point is not in dispute, and the argument in the משנה seems to lose its subject.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (one view)... Sets up a contrast with a view that has a problem.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rav:
this is what Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis argue about.
But according to Rabbi Yochanan,
about what do they argue?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב, בְּהָא פְּלִיגִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּנַן. אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב's answer and uses it to challenge רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even the חכמים agree that the leftover goat is rejected, then the dispute in the משנה has no clear subject according to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה's wording fits רב
steps.stepSummary: רבא admits the point. We already said that the precise wording of the משנה matches רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Didn't we already say that the משנה is exact according to רב?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not give רבי יוחנן an easy answer. He points out that we already know the משנה's wording leans toward רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of solving the problem for רבי יוחנן, רבא accepts that the משנה reads best according to רב. This means רבי יוחנן has to explain the משנה in a less natural way. After this, the גמרא turns to a new inference from the משנה, which will raise a difficulty for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise. A close reading of the wording supports this view.
Like him, in line with his view

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not answering for רבי יוחנן here. He is agreeing that the משנה is more naturally read like רב.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Didn't we say
that the Mishna is precise in accordance with Rav?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אָמְרִינַן דַּיְיקָא מַתְנִיתִין כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 10 by accepting that the משנה leans toward רב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No new explanation is offered. The משנה is admitted to fit רב better.

steps.title: Reading an inference from the משנה about a private sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a public sin-offering is not left to die. This implies that a private sin-offering in the same situation is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: because a public sin-offering is not left to die. This implies that a private sin-offering in a case like this is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and draws a hidden implication from its words. This sets up a new test of רב and רבי יוחנן in the next step, a test that will turn into a difficulty for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the חכמים' reason: a public חטאת is not left to die. By saying 'public,' it implies that a private חטאת in this same kind of case would be left to die. The גמרא will now check which view, רב or רבי יוחנן, can explain that implication, and this will turn into a challenge to רב.

phrases.english: We learned:
because a communal sin-offering is not left to die.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּיָחִיד כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא — מֵתָה.
phrases.english: This implies that an individual's in a case like this is left to die.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: שֶׁאֵין חַטַּאת צִבּוּר מֵתָה. הָא דְּיָחִיד כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא מֵתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line: an inference from the משנה about a private חטאת, which will be used to test רב and רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'שאין חטאת צבור מתה' we infer that a private חטאת in a comparable case is left to die.

steps.title: How רבי יוחנן explains the private case, introducing רבי אבא
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, the private sin-offering that dies fits a ruling of רבי אבא in the name of רב. The quote begins here and continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי יוחנן: this follows what רבי אבא said in the name of רב. For רבי אבא said in the name of רב:
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next move. The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן can explain the private case with a known ruling, and it starts quoting that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the leftover animal is rejected and is not offered. So a comparable private sin-offering being left to die matches an existing rule that רבי אבא reports from רב. The 'בשלמא' signals that רב's side will soon face a difficulty with this same inference.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the statement of רבי אבא
As he said. This introduces the full quote.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rabbi Yochanan:
it is in line with what Rabbi Abba said in the name of Rav.
As Rabbi Abba said in the name of Rav:
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, כִּדְרַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the inference of step 12 to רבי יוחנן first, before turning to רב.
steps.raayaObject: Showing that the private-offering inference fits רבי יוחנן easily, setting up a problem for רב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ruling of רבי אבא in the name of רב, whose content is quoted on the next amud
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that the surviving goat is not rejected
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי יוחנן, the private חטאת dying matches רבי אבא's rule that the first animal dies once atonement was made with the replacement. The 'בשלמא' signals that רב will be asked (on the next amud) how he explains it.
